entries.title: Uniform pressure approximation does not preserve a derivative jump
entries.statement: DRAFT; independent referee check pending. For every epsilon>0, P(x)=max(0,x) and Q_epsilon(x)=epsilon*log(1+exp(x/epsilon)), x in R, satisfy 0<Q_epsilon(x)-P(x)<=epsilon*log(2) uniformly. Q_epsilon is smooth and convex, with derivative 1/(1+exp(-x/epsilon)); hence arbitrarily small uniform convex-pressure approximation alone cannot force a derivative discontinuity. This functional counterexample does not disprove the nearest-neighbor Potts discontinuity conjecture, whose source target is positive critical magnetization.
assumptions: Comparison concerns uniform pressure error only
entries.domain: probability theory; Potts and random-cluster models

entries.title: The direct mean-field allowance does not exclude the q=3,d=3 saddle
entries.statement: DRAFT; independent referee check pending. Let F_J(x)=sum_i x_i*log(x_i)-(J/2)*sum_i x_i^2 on three-component probability vectors, J=4*log(2), u=(1/3,1/3,1/3), o=(2/3,1/6,1/6), s=(1/2,1/4,1/4). Then F_J(u)=F_J(o) and F_J(s)-F_J(u)=log(3)-(19/12)*log(2)>0. In the Biskup-Chayes extreme-state comparison, the allowed excess is J*(q-1)^2*I_d/(2*q), where I_d is the uniform integral of X^2/(1-X), X=(1/d)*sum_j cos(k_j). For d>=3, symmetry yields I_d>=1/(2*d). At q=3,d=3 this allowance is at least (4/9)*log(2), larger than the saddle excess, so this inequality alone does not exclude s. An upper error allowance exceeding this gap is not a lower bound on actual error and proves neither continuity nor impossibility of sharper methods. The comparison concerns extreme thermodynamic support pairs, not arbitrary Gibbs mixtures.
assumptions: The cited mean-field inequality must apply to the selected extreme thermodynamic state
entries.domain: probability theory; Potts and random-cluster models

entries.title: Positive finite FK boundary gaps can vanish exponentially
entries.statement: DRAFT; independent referee check pending. On a path of N>=3 edges with 0<p<1,q>1, compare free random-cluster boundary conditions with the boundary partition identifying the two endpoints. Put a=p/(p+q*(1-p)). The free law is iid Bernoulli(a). The endpoint-wired law is the free law tilted by 1+(q-1)*1{all N edges open}. Its open-edge marginal gap is rho_N=(q-1)*(1-a)*a^N/(1+(q-1)*a^N)>0, but rho_N tends to zero as N grows. Thus positive finite-volume boundary gaps alone do not establish a positive limiting witness. This path example does not disprove a claim for Z^d with d>=3.
assumptions: The only wiring identifies the path endpoints
entries.domain: probability theory; Potts and random-cluster models

entries.title: A fixed cylinder witness controls ordered edge marginal gaps
entries.statement: DRAFT; independent referee check pending. Let mu_0,mu_1 on {0,1}^E admit a monotone coupling X<=Y. For every finite F subset E and event A measurable on F, |mu_1(A)-mu_0(A)|<=sum_{e in F}(mu_1(omega_e)-mu_0(omega_e)). If the marginal difference is the same rho on every edge and |F|=M>=1, a fixed gap delta>0 implies rho>=delta/M. This uses a union bound on coordinate disagreements, with no independence assumption. Applying it in a volume limit requires fixed support and a gap bounded below uniformly in volume; growing M or vanishing delta can give a zero lower bound. For Potts discontinuity this does not construct the positive critical witness or identify pressure non-differentiability with the source's critical-magnetization target.
assumptions: F is finite and A depends only on F
A common marginal gap rho is needed for the delta/M conclusion
entries.domain: probability theory; Potts and random-cluster models

relations.rationale: The path example directly tests the volume-uniform positive-gap premise needed to instantiate the fixed-cylinder witness bound; it does not refute that conditional bound.

Both warn about transferring a phase jump through an approximation. The softplus example concerns uniform pressure error; the saddle calculation checks the stronger cited state-dependent mean-field allowance. Neither implies the other.
